newsitem.title: INDIA: India sugar prices up on lower quota announcements.
newsitem.headline: India sugar prices up on lower quota announcements.

text.p: Sugar prices rose on Wednesday on increased speculative buying after the annuouncement of lower government quotas for the coming months, dealers said.

In ready delivery, S-30 rose by 19/25 rupees to 1,264/1,300 rupees per quintal while M-30 moved up by 15/19 rupees to 1,290/1,355 rupees per quintal. Sugar mill delivery extended gains to 1,210/1,220 rupees per quintal from 1,185/1,200 rupees.

The Indian government has announced a free sale quota of 650,000 tonnes for January 1997 against the current month's 800,000 tonnes. Besides, it also extended the last date for selling December's quota from December 31 to January 10.
The quotas for February and March 1997 are 700,000 tonnes each. The quota for January 1996 had been 650,00 tonnes, while February and March had 625,000 each.
